analysis.evidence: שָׂפָה אֶחָת וּדְבָרִים אֲחָדִים describes the condition of כָל הָאָרֶץ at the opening of the narrative. The whole earth had one language and the same words.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces the Qal wayyiqtol יְהִי, third person masculine singular.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: כָל הָאָרֶץ means “the whole earth.” The shared language, שָׂפָה אֶחָת, shows that the phrase refers collectively to the earth’s inhabitants.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, with הָאָרֶץ as its complement.
